text: Marking the shared counter `volatile` still gave 533,401 instead of 1,600,000. Why?
choices: `volatile` fixes visibility of a single write; it does not make read-modify-write atomic, so the interleaving is unchanged.
`volatile` only applies to reference types, not to primitive `int` fields.
The JIT ignores `volatile` on fields it can prove are thread-local at the call site.
`volatile` guarantees atomicity only for 32-bit values on 64-bit processors.
explanation: Each step now sees fresh memory and the three steps are still three steps. The rule: `volatile` for visibility of a single write, never for read-modify-write. Its legitimate use is a flag one thread sets and another polls — without it the JIT may hoist the read out of the loop and the loop spins forever.
